verification_notes.subject: Three structural counts in the Gate 21 result
verification_notes.finding: The Gate 21 result reports 487 tool-level records, 298 distinct (server, tool) pairs, 189 duplicate observations, and TOOL=194. An independent recount from the same pinned files gives 315 dict-shaped tool records, 165 distinct pairs, and 22 TOOL records carrying a new_tool_config. The difference is entirely in the TOOL category: 194 counts every key inside a TOOL server entry, which comprises 89 addition_summary strings, 83 auto_optimizations lists, and 22 new_tool_config objects. Those are three different kinds of thing, and only the third is a tool record. PARAM=141 and DESC=152 agree exactly, as do total_bytes, server entries, all parameter counts, diff_hunks, and task_idx values.
verification_notes.consequence: The Gate 21 verdict (NOT AUDITABLE) and its reasoning are unaffected, and the decision-relevant count of 0 required parameter additions is confirmed exactly. But the conflated figures must not be quoted. The manuscript therefore reports server entries by mutation_type, parameter items, diff hunks, and new tool configurations, each with its unit named, and does not use the 487 / 298 / 189 / 194 figures at all.

verification_notes.subject: Gate 19 Path A
verification_notes.finding: Gate 19 concluded that public MCP-evolution benchmarks published no old/new correspondence register, having examined the task file and declined a 3.4 GB archive. The recommendation is narrowed from 'publish the register' to 'normalize the correspondence into old and new argument sets carrying the expected target value', which is what the failed conversion actually shows to be missing.

verification_notes.subject: The reproduction claim of section 8 did not hold for a reader
verification_notes.finding: Section 8 of version 3 stated that scripts/reproduce.py 'exits zero with the audit artifacts byte-identical to the committed files'. Checking out gate22-paper-v3-20260914 into a fresh working tree and running the harness there exited 1. Two independent causes. (a) 48 paths have their SHA-256 asserted inside a committed artifact; cloning on Windows with the Git-for-Windows default core.autocrlf=true rewrote all of them, failing stage 2 and the stage 4 register_sha256 comparison. (b) 87 of the 134 frozen manifest entries are the raw Gate 07/08 measurement archive under gates/artifacts/, about 107 MB, excluded by gates/artifacts/.gitignore and carried by no tag; no clone has ever been able to check them. The defect was in the claim and in the repository packaging, not in any measurement.
verification_notes.resolution: Added .gitattributes pinning exactly the 48 hash-asserted paths with -text; a blanket policy was rejected because 191 of 602 tracked files hold CRLF on disk against an LF blob. Stage 2 now distinguishes a file that is present but altered (always a failure) from one that was never distributed, reports PASS (PARTIAL) with the reason, and records the partial state in its summary; --require-full-manifest restores strict behaviour. Section 8 rewritten to state stage by stage what a clone can and cannot verify, and REPRODUCE.md rewritten, having still described 4 stages, 6 tests and a 'negative control'.
verification_notes.impact_on_measured_values: None. No reachability number depends on the undistributed archive: the 310-item register is rebuilt from the committed generator, so stages 3 and 5 are byte-identical from a bare clone. Verified after the change: fresh clone with core.autocrlf=true runs all five stages and exits 0; owner working tree still reports 134/134 UNCHANGED. The 87 undistributed entries remain hash-attested in public through the committed frozen manifest, which records their SHA-256 and byte size.
verification_notes.found_by: Verification of the gate22-paper-v3-20260914 tag during version 3.1 preparation, 2026-09-16. Not found by the version 2 external review, which read only the package ZIP.

verification_notes.subject: Eight frozen artifacts had stopped hashing to their own frozen manifest
verification_notes.finding: GATE_07_METRICS.json, GATE_07_METRICS_V4.json, GATE_07_PROTOCOL.json, GATE_07_PROTOCOL_V2.json, GATE_07_PROTOCOL_V3.json, GATE_07_PROTOCOL_V4.json, GATE_07_PROTOCOL_V4_FREEZE_LEDGER.json and GATE_08_PROTOCOL.json, all under gates/baselines/, had been normalised to LF by Git at an earlier commit. Their committed bytes therefore did not hash to the value gates/results/GATE_19_FROZEN_SOURCE_HASHES.json records for them. The working tree still matched, which is why every prior run passed: the repository verified only on the machine that produced it. For GATE_07_PROTOCOL_V2.json the original mixed endings, 389 CRLF and 4 bare LF, are not reconstructible from the blob by any eol setting.
verification_notes.resolution: The bytes of the eight were restored to the form the frozen manifest was taken over, and all 48 hash-asserted paths pinned with -text so no checkout can rewrite them again. The frozen manifest itself was NOT edited: the artifacts were moved back to the manifest, not the manifest to the artifacts.
verification_notes.impact_on_measured_values: None. For each of the eight the parsed JSON before and after is identical and the only difference is line endings; this was asserted file by file before the change was staged. After the restoration all 47 tracked manifest entries hash to their recorded values from the committed blobs.

verification_notes.subject: A third-party figure was quoted against the wrong denominator
verification_notes.finding: Section 2.1 of manuscript versions 3, 3.1 and 3.2 read 'Wang et al. run an agentic auditor over 168 benchmarks in nine domains and find over 25.7% carrying critical issues'. The subject of that sentence is the benchmark count, so it reads as 25.7% of 168 benchmarks. The abstract of arXiv:2605.26079 states the figure as a share of tasks: 'critical issues including ambiguous task design, execution environment conflicts, and incorrect ground truths in over 25.7% of the evaluated tasks'. The supporting_quote recorded for this reference in REFERENCES_VERIFIED.json was itself a paraphrase presented in a quotes field, and it had already dropped 'of the evaluated tasks'. The paraphrase is what carried the error from the verification record into the manuscript.
verification_notes.resolution: The manuscript sentence now attributes the figure to the evaluated tasks and the emphasis is explicit. The supporting_quotes entry in REFERENCES_VERIFIED.json was replaced with the verbatim abstract sentence, and a correction_v33 field records what the paraphrase had said.
verification_notes.impact_on_measured_values: None. No number produced by this project derives from or is compared against this figure; it is contextual.
verification_notes.found_by: External review of the version 3.2 package, 2026-09-16. Re-verified here against the arXiv abstract page on the same date.
verification_notes.class: Same class as V11 and V12 and as the risk-register error the paper reports in section 5.5: a paraphrase that nobody re-read against the source, surviving three releases inside the artifact whose purpose is to prevent exactly that.

verification_notes.subject: Appendix A contradicted the declared grammar it was meant to summarise
verification_notes.finding: Version 3 declared the complete five-rule grammar in research/gate19/derivation_grammar.json and disclosed in section 4.1 that the auditor does not parse an arbitrary rights policy, because the builders materialise the rights ahead of the audit. Appendix A was not updated to match either change. Its step 1 still said 'Parse the declared information-rights object', contradicting section 4.1, and its step 3 listed only identity, visible_split and declared_external_derivation, omitting visible_literal - the undeclared rule that section 3.3 reports firing 35 times. A reader treating Appendix A as the algorithm specification would have found the paper contradicting itself on the two points version 3 existed to repair.
verification_notes.resolution: Appendix A was rewritten to the evaluation_order recorded in research/gate19/derivation_grammar.json: target_field_declared, target_value_present, identity, visible_literal, unobservable_join, visible_split, declared_external_derivation, fail_closed. The rewrite states that unobservable_join is evaluated before visible_split and that the order is therefore load-bearing, which the previous four-step summary did not express at all, and it states that no item in the frozen register is both an unobservable join and a visible split.
verification_notes.impact_on_measured_values: None. The implementation was already correct and unchanged; the defect was in the appendix. gates/results/GATE_19_AUDIT.json is untouched.
verification_notes.found_by: External review of the version 3.2 package, 2026-09-16. The corrected rule order was taken from the committed grammar artifact and checked against research/gate19/auditor.py::classify_item rather than from the review, which proposed an order placing the convention check after the admission rules. That order would have been a second mismatch: the implementation evaluates unobservable_join between visible_literal and visible_split.
verification_notes.class: Declaration drift, as in V09 and V10. No measured value moved.
